set.body:
## Objective

Determine whether one uncertainty-guided patch refresh during rigid Flashalign refinement improves landmark accuracy or reduces complete runtime at a fixed accuracy level after charging every scouting cost.

Treat the data curvature as a local observability and Monte Carlo allocation signal. Adaptive importance sampling may reduce estimation error in weak motion directions; it does not create information absent from the fixed population objective.

## Experimental scope

Implement a benchmark-only rigid experiment before changing any production preset or public API.

1. Start from the current quality-weighted optimization draw.
2. At the first scheduled rigid checkpoint, form the data-only generalized eigensystem H v = lambda D v, where H is projected-patch Gauss-Newton curvature and D is the fixed-probe physical displacement metric.
3. Define a weak eigenspace rather than relying on one unstable smallest eigenvector.
4. Score a modest candidate pool using nuisance-projected patch Jacobians, fixed-support validity, contrast margin, capped robust reliability, and leverage clipping.
5. Draw one refreshed optimization set from a positive mixture of the existing broad distribution and the adaptive priority.
6. Preserve the target population weights with q_p divided by M Q pi_p. Freeze sample IDs, probabilities, objective weights, contrast gates, polarity priors, and robust-loss parameters throughout each trust-region block.
7. Keep selection fixed for all candidate comparisons and keep audit sealed until final model selection.

The experiment must preserve the specialized six-parameter rigid path. Affine, PE, small-strain, velocity, HalfFlow, and user-facing controls are out of scope.

## Required comparison

Use three paired arms with identical initial samples, initialization, checkpoint timing, selection samples, audit samples, and restart behavior:

- current frozen optimization sample;
- ordinary quality-weighted refresh;
- weak-direction adaptive refresh.

The ordinary-refresh arm is the primary comparator. It separates directional allocation from the generic benefit of seeing a new random sample.

## Numerical and mechanism gates

1. On an exactly enumerable patch population, adaptive probabilities and importance weights reproduce the target loss, gradient, and curvature in expectation.
2. Equivalent physical representations, including axis permutation and parameter rescaling, yield equivalent weak subspaces and sampling priorities.
3. Every patch retains positive draw probability. Near-threshold contrast, incomplete support, low current inlier probability, repeated draws, and tied eigenspaces remain finite and deterministic.
4. Sample refresh changes the objective identity, resets its current value, and forces relinearization. No raw optimization loss is compared across sample-set identities.
5. On a directional phantom with localized identifying structure, adaptive refresh reduces weak-direction curvature or gradient estimator variance by at least 25 percent at equal fixed-image evaluation work.
6. On a truly rotation-symmetric phantom, the method retains an insufficient-information outcome and does not manufacture apparent identifiability.

## Held-out acceptance criterion

Compare adaptive refresh with the ordinary-refresh arm using subjects as the paired bootstrap unit and sampling seeds nested within subjects. Include every failed run in the original denominator.

Accept an accuracy gain only if all conditions hold:

- complete median wall-clock time, including scouting, is no more than 5 percent higher;
- median landmark RMS error is at least 10 percent lower;
- the one-sided 95 percent paired bootstrap confidence bound for the landmark-error ratio is below 1.0;
- landmark p95 and catastrophic-failure rate do not worsen;
- benefit is present in the intended directional-structure or partial-coverage strata rather than only in easy cases.

Alternatively, accept a cost gain if median and p95 landmark error and failure rate are statistically noninferior while complete median runtime falls by at least 15 percent.

Optimized patch loss, sampled conditioning, or the methods own information diagnostic cannot satisfy the acceptance criterion.

## Cost and evidence accounting

Record scouting candidates, unique interpolations, gradient samples, source voxel reads, compiled patch entries, linearizations, trials, selections, audit work, allocations, rigid-phase time, and complete pipeline time. Interleave timed arms in the same environment and retain exact fixture, configuration, seed, platform, JVM, and source identities.

Match deterministic fixed-image work for the primary comparison and report complete wall time separately. Do not tune the scouting-pool size, mixture weight, weak-space threshold, clipping, or checkpoint on held-out cases.

## Decision rule

Retain the mechanism only if it satisfies one held-out acceptance route against the ordinary-refresh comparator and does not regress the frozen-sample control materially. If gains disappear after scouting cost, occur only in internal diagnostics, or arise equally from an ordinary refresh, close the epic as a successful falsification with production behavior unchanged.

A positive result authorizes a separate production-integration decision. Completion of this epic alone does not change defaults, presets, APIs, or release claims.

## Planned paths

Reserve exact paths only when implementation begins. Expected experimental scope:

- benchmarks/flashalign/
- benchmark-local code under the reframe4s.flashalign package
- focused shared tests only where needed to prove unbiased weighting or physical weak-space semantics

Changes to modules/reframe4s-flashalign production sources require a separate preflight and must remain additive and disabled by default.
set.title: EPIC: Flashalign weak-direction adaptive patch sampling experiment
